video.label: Megan Rembielak / Tanner Tees - Two Tee Extension Drill

extraction.overallNotes: Megan Rembielak demonstrates a double-tee hitting drill aimed at maintaining barrel extension through the hitting zone post-contact to prevent premature rollover.

claims.claimText: Extending the bat barrel through the hitting zone after contact optimizes power and directional ball flight while preventing premature wrist rollover.
claims.sourceProposition: Extension after contact keeps the barrel through the tunnel toward the pitcher, maximizing power and helping direct the ball rather than rolling over into weak grounders.
claims.observableEvidence: Observation of bat barrel path continuing forward toward the pitcher after contact with extended arms prior to the finish roll-over.
claims.appliesWhen: Executing swing follow-through and extension on pitches through the middle of the zone.
claims.doesNotApplyWhen: Adjusting to extreme inside pitch locations where hand path must clear tightly.
claims.qualityNotes: Standard mechanical coaching concept for swing extension and barrel control.
claims.causeVsSymptomNote: Premature wrist roll is often a symptom of poor barrel path or rotational casting.
claims.coachingCue: Drive the barrel through the tunnel from home to the pitcher.
claims.levelScopeNote: Applicable across all age groups learning proper post-contact extension.

drills.name: Two Tee Extension Drill
drills.targetedProblem: Pulling the bat barrel out of the hitting zone too early and rolling over prematurely into ground balls.
